associations: Current verdict: on the existing witness logs, H1 does not yet exhibit a compact witness taxonomy that is genuinely more specific than Ford-style local divisor/product coverage; the visible structure mostly looks like generic local product coverage with one thin endogenous decoration.

The only recurring T-specific motif that clearly survives late record gaps is the single skipped value witnessed as 1 * previous_column_term; in the late million-step records this axis-1 witness is exactly the previous column border term and it covers only one value per interval.
Late record gaps are increasingly composite-only events, so prime-side assignment is not carrying the mechanism: record gaps 17, 20, 21, 28, and 30 contain zero skipped primes.

Witness multiplicity stays sparse even in the largest observed intervals: in the million-step run, multiplicity-1 witnesses account for about 65.5% to 89.5% of skipped values in the record gaps 19, 20, 21, 25, 28, and 30.

The candidate compact taxonomy degrades as gaps grow: the share of skipped values whose chosen witness has min(row_factor, column_factor) <= 10 drops from about 50% at gap 19 to about 34.5% at gap 30, while the share with min factor > 100 rises from about 5.6% to about 44.8%.

That trend matters because a real compact certificate would usually become more low-dimensional as the interval grows; here the visible witnesses become more balanced, more idiosyncratic, and less small-factor driven.

Ford's multiplication-table and divisor-in-an-interval papers remain the closest overlap branch because the current logs mostly certify that each skipped integer has some factor pair in the local border product set, not that the mex coupling creates a qualitatively new certificate language.

Practical-number and dense-divisor theory supply the right standard of compactness: those theories give short interval-extension criteria for complete local coverage, whereas the current T logs only show heterogeneous pointwise witnesses.

Numerical-semigroup and numerical-monoid factorization invariants are a plausible rescue route because they compress heterogeneous factorizations by graph-level invariants rather than by exact factor identities.

Symbolic-dynamics and S-gap-shift analogies remain possible only after quotienting witnesses into mesoscopic signatures; the raw witness stream itself does not look finite-alphabet or substitution-like.

Parking-process and random-sequential-adsorption analogies are better as phenomenology for vacancy clusters than as witness taxonomies; they may model gap lengths, but they do not by themselves separate T-specific certificates from generic local coverage.

The main caveat is that the record-gap corpus stores only one explicit witness per skipped integer plus a multiplicity count; that is enough to make H1 look weak, but not enough to prove that all-witness hypergraphs lack a sharper compressible invariant.

forced_bridges.mechanism: Treat a record interval as a local coverage problem and ask whether a short ordered chain of small border factors extends coverage interval-by-interval, analogous to Stewart-Sierpinski style interval extension. If no short chain exists, then the logs are closer to generic divisor-in-an-interval coverage than to a compact T-specific certificate.

View each skipped value as an element of a dynamically generated multiplicative monoid and replace raw witnesses by factorization invariants such as catenary-like distance, Betti-type branching, or Apéry-frontier coordinates. A compact invariant profile could exist even if exact factor pairs are heterogeneous.

Model each interval as a hypergraph whose vertices are skipped integers and whose hyperedges are border factors or factor-pair templates. Compactness then becomes bounded description length, low VC-dimension, or low treewidth of the witness hypergraph rather than repeated exact factorizations.

Encode each skipped value by a coarse witness signature such as axis, tiny-factor, mesoscopic-factor, balanced-singleton, or redundant-balanced, then test whether the resulting word is generated by a finite automaton, substitution, or low-complexity shift. Failure would support collapse of H1 at the symbolic level too.

Interpret uncovered integers as vacancies and each mex update as leftmost-vacancy repair. This does not solve witness taxonomy directly, but it creates a control question: if gap lengths look jammed while witnesses remain heterogeneous, then gap boundedness and witness compressibility are separate issues.

anomaly_results.constraint: Zero skipped primes inside a record gap
anomaly_results.result: Large record gaps still occur with no skipped primes at all. In the million-step run, record gaps 17, 20, 21, 28, and 30 are composite-only intervals.
anomaly_results.implication: Any H1 variant that leans on prime-side assignment as the main witness taxonomy is too weak; the dominant mechanism must explain composite coverage directly.

anomaly_results.constraint: Ask for a T-specific witness class that recurs in every large record interval
anomaly_results.result: Exactly one such class is obvious in the current logs: the single axis-1 witness, and in late records it is exactly the previous column term lying inside the row-gap interval.
anomaly_results.implication: This is a real endogenous feature, but it is too thin to explain interval-wide coverage. It looks like a boundary marker, not a certificate language.

anomaly_results.constraint: Demand redundancy as evidence of a stable certificate family
anomaly_results.result: Redundancy is limited. For the late records 19, 20, 21, 25, 28, and 30, multiplicity-1 coverage accounts for about 83.3%, 89.5%, 80.0%, 75.0%, 66.7%, and 65.5% of skipped values respectively.
anomaly_results.implication: The witness corpus is dominated by brittle pointwise coverage, so there is little evidence that long gaps are sustained by a reusable redundant template.

anomaly_results.constraint: Force witnesses to stay in a tiny-factor language
anomaly_results.result: That language decays with scale. The proportion of skipped values whose chosen witness has min factor <= 10 falls from about 50% at gap 19 to about 34.5% at gap 30, while the min-factor > 100 bucket rises to about 44.8% at gap 30.
anomaly_results.implication: A low-factor certificate grammar is not stable across larger record gaps. The visible witnesses drift toward generic balanced factorizations.

anomaly_results.constraint: Use the current logs alone to decide H1 conclusively
anomaly_results.result: The logs are informative but lossy because each skipped value stores one witness plus multiplicity, not the full witness set.
anomaly_results.implication: The current evidence strongly disfavors a compact raw-witness taxonomy, but the only serious rescue is to find compression in the full witness hypergraph or in a higher-level invariant.

steering_directions.direction: Log full witness hypergraphs for record gaps, not just one witness plus multiplicity.
steering_directions.rationale: If H1 survives, the compression is likely hidden in the structure of all factor pairs rather than in the first witness picked by the generator. The present corpus is already strong enough to make raw-witness H1 look weak, but not strong enough to rule out higher-order compression.
steering_directions.first_step: Extend the generator so that for each skipped integer in each record interval it stores every admissible border factor pair up to the current frontier, then derive graph summaries per value and per interval.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Either a small family of interval-level graph motifs repeats across late records, or motif diversity explodes and H1 collapses cleanly into generic local product coverage.

steering_directions.direction: Test a practical-number style interval-extension criterion on the border sets.
steering_directions.rationale: Practical and dense-divisor theories are the clearest examples of genuinely compact local coverage certificates. If the prime-separator array has a T-specific certificate, it should resemble a short interval-extension chain rather than a long list of heterogeneous factorizations.
steering_directions.first_step: For each record interval, sort the available border factors up to the square-root scale and test whether a short initial segment already forces complete coverage of almost all skipped values by interval extension inequalities.
steering_directions.expected_signal: A short chain of low factors certifies most of the interval with only one or two T-specific exceptions; if not, the witness story remains Ford-like local coverage.

steering_directions.direction: Run a generic-control ablation against size-matched surrogate product sets.
steering_directions.rationale: The core novelty question is comparative: are the witness logs more compressible than ordinary local product coverage? Without a control, H1 risks renaming generic divisor-in-an-interval behavior.
steering_directions.first_step: Construct surrogates that preserve the row and column marginal size profiles or small-factor histograms but destroy mex coupling, then compare record-interval witness compression, singleton rate, and balanced-factor share.
steering_directions.expected_signal: If T-specific structure is real, the true process should show materially lower description length or a more stable signature inventory than the surrogates.

steering_directions.direction: Replace raw witness labels by factorization invariants inspired by numerical monoids.
steering_directions.rationale: Exact factor identities are too heterogeneous. A compact witness taxonomy, if it exists, may live at the level of factorization-graph invariants such as branching, distance between factorizations, or Apéry-like frontier coordinates.
steering_directions.first_step: On the full-witness corpus, compute per-value invariants including multiplicity, smallest factor bucket, largest factor bucket, balancedness, axis participation, and graph connectivity between factorizations.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Late record gaps share a low-dimensional invariant signature even when the explicit factor pairs differ wildly.

steering_directions.direction: Probe a mesoscopic symbolic language instead of a literal witness taxonomy.
steering_directions.rationale: The raw witness stream does not look finite-alphabet, but a bucketed signature stream might. This is the last plausible route to a compact certificate language that is still more specific than Ford-style local coverage.
steering_directions.first_step: Encode each skipped value by a coarse signature such as axis-marker, tiny-factor singleton, tiny-factor redundant, balanced singleton, or balanced redundant, then test compression and predictive cross-entropy on later record gaps.
steering_directions.expected_signal: If a low-complexity symbolic law exists, the bucketed stream will compress substantially better than shuffled or surrogate controls; otherwise the symbolic rescue fails.

validation_checks.check: Measure motif growth as record gaps increase: number of distinct interval-level witness graphs, number of distinct per-value factorization signatures, and description length per skipped value.
validation_checks.success_signal: These quantities stabilize or grow sublinearly across late record gaps, showing genuine compression beyond the first-witness logs.
validation_checks.failure_signal: They grow roughly proportionally with interval length, confirming that H1 collapses into generic local coverage.

validation_checks.check: For each record interval, ask how many of the smallest available border factors are needed before interval-extension inequalities force coverage of the whole skipped block.
validation_checks.success_signal: A uniformly bounded or very slowly growing prefix of factors explains most late record gaps.
validation_checks.failure_signal: The required factor set keeps expanding and still leaves many balanced singleton cases unexplained.

validation_checks.check: Compare the true process against surrogates on singleton share, balanced-factor share, axis-marker frequency, and compressed signature length.
validation_checks.success_signal: The true process is significantly more compressible or shows a distinctive invariant profile absent from the surrogates.
validation_checks.failure_signal: The surrogates match the observed statistics closely, which means the current witness story is not more specific than Ford-style local coverage.

validation_checks.check: Cluster skipped values and record intervals using invariant vectors rather than exact factors, then test whether the clusters remain stable when the computation horizon increases from 30k to 200k to 1M steps.
validation_checks.success_signal: A small number of invariant clusters persists and predicts later records.
validation_checks.failure_signal: Cluster count and predictive error both keep growing, showing that the invariants are not compressing the witness data.

validation_checks.check: Train finite-state or substitution-style models on the bucketed signature stream and compare out-of-sample cross-entropy against shuffled and Markov baselines.
validation_checks.success_signal: The symbolic model materially outperforms the baselines on later record gaps.
validation_checks.failure_signal: No model beats simple baselines, so the apparent witness buckets are descriptive only and not a genuine compact law.

sub_problem: Do the record-gap intervals in the prime-separator array admit a compact witness taxonomy that is genuinely more specific than Ford-style local divisor/product coverage, or do the witness logs show that H1 collapses into generic local product coverage?
